name: Finch Arboretum
title: Ancient Trees in Finch Arboretum, Spokane: 6 Worth Finding
meta_description: A state champion willow, two of America's first dawn redwoods, and a linden planted by the family who gave the ground: 6 trees in Finch Arboretum.
intro: John A. Finch Arboretum grew from land a pioneer family gave the city, and six of Spokane's most remarkable trees now stand within a few hundred metres of each other inside it. Daniel H. Dwight's own family provided part of the original ground, and a Hungarian linden planted in his name still grows there. The state's largest white willow is here too, started as somebody's garden tree before the ground became a public arboretum, growing beside two of the first dawn redwoods ever brought to North America, seed-grown after a stand once known only from fossils turned up alive in China in 1943. A Miyabe maple, modest by its own species but the largest recorded in Washington, a Norway spruce the city calls its second tallest, and a broad Mexican pinyon pine round out the six. The arboretum is free, open daily, and every one of these trees sits inside a single short walk.
